resources.string: To find other devices over Bluetooth, Android versions before 12 require the location permission. The app does not determine or store your location — this is a system requirement for BLE scanning.
Broadcasting and scanning over Bluetooth needs the “Nearby devices” permission. Location is not requested.
Discovery cannot work without Bluetooth. It will resume on its own once you turn it on.
This device’s Bluetooth chip cannot do BLE advertising. You will see other users, but they will not see you.
Discovery works without them, but the persistent notification with the counter will not be shown.
No encounters yet. Turn discovery on and keep your phone with you — other StreetPass users will show up here.
No nickname set — only the ID is broadcast. You can set one in Settings.
The ID is all your phone sends: 8 random bytes not tied to you, your account or your device. Other users count encounters with you by it. It can be changed in Settings.
History is empty.\n\nTurn discovery on from the Home tab and keep your phone with you. As soon as another StreetPass user with the app running is nearby, the encounter will appear here.
Shown to other users instead of your ID
The nickname is broadcast in the clear: anyone with a Bluetooth scanner nearby can read it. Leave it empty to stay fully anonymous.
Lets other users count an encounter with you
Scan the air and record encounters
If discovery was on, bring it back up when the system starts
8 seconds of scanning every 2 minutes. Longest battery life, but passing encounters may be missed.
10 seconds of scanning every minute. A sensible compromise for everyday carry.
Continuous scanning. Misses nothing, noticeably drains the battery.
A repeat encounter with the same person counts no sooner than %1$s later
During that time the person may be nearby and the signal received, but no new encounter is added to the history. Range: %1$d–%2$d minutes.
only up close, within half a metre
maximum range, including neighbours behind a wall

Packets weaker than the threshold are dropped, so people behind a wall or a floor below are not counted. The closer to −40, the closer the person has to be. The distance estimate is rough and depends on the phone.

What is collected: the random 8-byte ID of each device met, its nickname if it broadcasts one, the time of the encounter and, if enabled below, the signal strength.\n\nWhat is not collected: location, MAC addresses, device names, contacts, anything about you. Everything stays on this phone: the app only goes online to check for updates when you ask it to, and it is excluded from cloud backup.
RSSI in the history helps judge how close the person was
Other users will start seeing you as a new person: at the next encounter they will record a “first meeting”. Your own history is unaffected.
All encounters and statistics will be deleted permanently. Discovery keeps running.
Checking is the only reason the app needs internet: a single request to GitHub when you tap the button. It contains nothing about your encounters or your ID.
You have the latest version (on GitHub: %1$s).
